ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

payload.proof_nl: Let x be any real number. By definition of the floor function, m := floor(x) is an integer such that m <= x < m + 1. Define f := x - m. Then f >= 0 because x >= m, and f < 1 because x < m + 1. By the usual definition of the fractional part, frac(x) = x - floor(x) = x - m = f. Therefore x = m + f = floor(x) + frac(x), and also 0 <= frac(x) < 1. Since x was arbitrary, the statement holds for every real number x.
payload.role_in_assembly: Provide the canonical decomposition of an arbitrary real number into an integer part and a fractional part.
